newsitem.title: USA: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. weekly rice cash market summary -- USDA.

text.p: In the southern United States rice prices were steady in the week ended April 19, USDA Market News said in its weekly update.

Long grain milled rice prices were selling mostly at $20.50 to $21.00 per hundred pounds (CWT); Medium grain traded mostly at $19.00; Second heads were 50 cents lower and Brewers remain in very tight supply with a few quotes at $13.75-15.00.
Rice by-products were uneven with bran was mostly steady and millfeed also mostly steady to $4.00 higher.
In California, rice prices were steady with medium grain selling mostly from $18.00-19.00. Second heads were $1.00-2.00 lower and bran was unevenly $3.00 lower to $5.00 higher.

California rice ship loadings for the week ending April 19, 1997: at the Port of Sacramento the Sea Dream loaded 21,455 tonnes of U.S. No. 1 medium grain milled bulk rice destined for Turkey and the Apollo loaded 20,000 tonnes for Jordan.

Inspections of California rice for export for the week ending April 19: there were 914,325 cwt of medium grain milled rice inspected. The season total since October 1, 1996, was 9,476,475 cwt compared to 6,178,783 cwt inspected a year ago.
